data.why: The repo's own sample FASTA (4 ancient-DNA fragments) covers base-composition/ORF/codon exploration and multi-sequence comparison; a second written file adds a mutated variant and an ambiguous-base (N) edge case for mutation-comparison and validation testing.

goals: Upload or paste a DNA sequence and read off its base composition, GC content, and AT/GC and purine/pyrimidine ratios
Scan a sequence for open reading frames and estimate candidate protein lengths
Examine codon usage bias and six-frame protein translations for a sequence
Compute GC skew and sliding-window GC content to spot compositional shifts along a sequence
Find restriction enzyme cut sites in a sequence
Compare two sequences position-by-position to tally point mutations, transitions, and transversions

review.summary: This is a faithful, well-shaped tree: its five phases match the app's input sidebar and four pages, the checker agrees on every task and feature, and the general labels would carry over to other tools. It needs a few fixes before filing, mainly the misread of the 50-row-capped mutation table on screens/032.webp, the missing note that the comparison doesn't align sequences, a wrong 'one-of' branch, and one missing composition-charts feature.
